sanskrit_verse:
भ्रातरः संविभक्ता ये स्वरुच्या तु परस्परम् ।
विभागपत्रं कुर्वन्ति भागलेख्यं तद् उच्यते ॥
transliteration:
bhrātaraḥ saṃvibhaktā ye svarucyā tu parasparam /
vibhāgapatraṃ kurvanti bhāgalekhyaṃ tad ucyate //
sph_interpretive_translation: When brothers, though divided by personal inclination, mutually execute a document of division, it is declared as Bhāgalekhyam.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in mutual consent, not coercive imposition
Causation arises from conscious choice, not external compulsion
Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of intent and autonomy
Restoration logic affirms relational harmony over material partition
Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of shared origin
executable_legal_axioms: IF parties are blood-related AND voluntarily sign a division document THEN recognize Bhāgalekhyam as valid without punitive oversight
IF division arises from svārthadarśana (self-view) THEN initiate capacity-restoration protocol to reaffirm unity-consciousness
IF no coercion is present THEN validate transactional outcome regardless of economic equality
IF Vibhāgapatram contains mutual attestation THEN enforce completion process to ensure energetic closure
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, Bhāgalekhyam shall be recognized at face value when established through voluntary execution. The court shall affirm the document's validity based on conscious consent rather than assessing fairness or equity. Responsibility lies in honoring the act of mutual declaration.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that division stems from individual will, not wrongdoing. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that separation manifests sequentially from internal divergence, not imposed conflict. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of conscious participation. Non-punitive reality rule establishes that no harm accrues from lawful self-determination.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Ensure all parties acknowledge the Vibhāgapatram as a conscious act of self-definition
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Confirm each brother accepts full ownership of their decision and its consequences
Capacity Restoration: Offer access to spiritual practices to restore unity-consciousness post-partition
Integrity Reintegration: Facilitate periodic review meetings to maintain relational coherence despite physical division
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this Dharma is declared. Justice flows from consciousness alignment, not punitive reaction. Division executed in awareness restores integrity to both self and relation. Reality responds to truth, not judgment.
